nodes.speaker: sci
nodes.text: Two landing sites: a sunlit ridge with near-constant sun, or the shadowed edge of a crater next to ancient ice. Where to?

variants.text: Dr. Okafor hugs her science rack: the shadowed crater edge is right beside ancient ice! Or take the sunlit ridge?

nodes.fact: The Moon's south pole has peaks lit almost all the time and craters that haven't seen sunlight for billions of years, where ice may hide.

nodes.speaker: ops
nodes.text: Time to fire the descent engine. A gentle descent leaves time to hover. A steep one saves fuel.

variants.text: Time to fire the descent engine. The rough orbit burn used extra fuel, so margins are thin.
Time to fire the descent engine. Our tidy orbit left a comfortable fuel margin.

nodes.fact: A lander must slow from about 1.6 km per second to a gentle stop, so fuel is the biggest part of its weight.

nodes.speaker: eng
nodes.text: Fuel warning! At this rate we have under a minute of hover time.

variants.text: Fuel warning! Under a minute of hover time. Dropping the heavy science rack would help, but Dr. Okafor won't like it.

nodes.fact: Apollo 11 landed with only about 25 seconds of fuel to spare. Dumping weight is an old trick for stretching fuel.
